render_contract: stages[] mirrors the instrument schema.html `const P` stage contract {eng,engname,sub,name,table,tag,what,why,logic,status{},example{},fields[{field,type,desc,tier,state,allowed,vset,caveat}],irr{primary,touches},code,split{always,drawer}}. design-SB: render library-schema.html FROM this artifact — NEVER hardcode (§2.13/§2.16). Layers: 1 OVERVIEW (always: what/why/logic→mermaid/status) · 2 WORKED EXAMPLE (always: example.row + example.tests) · DATA CONTRACT (drawer: fields grouped by tier key/supporting/plumbing/dormant) · AUDIT (drawer: irr) · IMPLEMENTATION (drawer: code). split{} names the always-visible vs drawer keys per stage.
mermaid_convention: the `logic` line is 'IN: … → BOX: … → OUT: … → NEXT: …'. design-SB renders it deterministically as a 3-node flow input(IN)→engine(BOX)→output(OUT) with a NEXT edge label — so a new drawer needs no new HTML, only a logic line in this shape.
ssot: https://grammarofmeaning.org/engine/schema.html (the INSTRUMENT SSOT, §2.16) — this library page is its sibling for the STOCK; both render from a registry, neither is hardcoded.

stages.name: The stock we hold
stages.what: The corpus is every primary source the project holds — books, articles, sermons, oral-history recordings, artworks — plus the passages (L4 anchors) chunked out of them. It is not a pipeline stage; it is the stock every engine reads.
stages.why: A source is a container, a passage is the analytical atom (the L4 anchor the instrument codes). Counting sources tells you collection COVERAGE, not analytical DEPTH — so the corpus reports an honest 3-part count (registered / held-as-full-text / reference) rather than one flattering headline (§2.8, the anti-inflation discipline).
stages.logic: IN: a harvested artifact + its provenance → BOX: register a `sources` row (provenance triad, tradition binding, dedup), then chunk at native divisions into L4 `passages` → OUT: held full text + quotable L4 anchors → NEXT: SERVE hands them to the instrument.

stages.name: Classify → route → resolve → dedup → gateway
stages.tag: how a needed source is located + landed
stages.what: CRADLE is the ONE pipeline every discovered source routes through: a classifier tags the input, a cluster router fans it out (BOOK/ACADEMIC/SCRIPTURE/ORAL/LITERARY/MANUSCRIPT), a resolver chain tries endpoints in priority order, a dedup check runs, and the ingestion gateway lands it. PRISM classifies the endpoints (13 routing axes); FOUNDRY casts firing harvesters from them.
stages.why: The load-bearing rule is the Parity Principle (§2.10): an endpoint is routed by what it CONTAINS, never by which tradition it 'serves'. An African journal on St. Paul fires for ANY Pauline query with the same priority as a US one — so the corpus's Anglophone default is corrected at routing, not hidden by curatorial pre-filtering (§2.8 enforced mechanically).
stages.logic: IN: a citation / keyword / bibliography item → BOX: classify → fan to matching clusters (Parity: geo_origin is never a filter) → try resolvers ≥0.5 → dedup vs sources+canonical → OUT: a landed source via the gateway (provenance + tradition binding) → NEXT: it becomes CORPUS.

status.limit: The health columns are DEFAULT-INFLATED: 3,201 rows read 'healthy' but last_audit_firing_rate_pct>0 for 0 of them — the audit-firing column is entirely unpopulated. Per the S94 funnel-state ~134 endpoints ACTUALLY yield. 'built+healthy' is an aspiration column, not a measured one (§2.7 data-quality gap).

stages.name: Recall vs a named authority
stages.tag: the library audits its own silence
stages.what: LACUNA is the reflexive turn: the library measures what it is MISSING by set-difference against a clavis — a named external authority that enumerates a literature (e.g. Syriaca.org's Syriac authors). 'Missing' stops meaning 'a machine didn't recall it' and starts meaning 'a named scholarly authority attests this and we hold no witness.'
stages.why: This is what makes the corpus's blindness DEFENSIBLE rather than embarrassing (§2.8). Every silence carries the authority's own citation (a clavis_number), so a third party who is NOT us can check it. The auditor never enumerates from memory — the gate is 'no memory-enumeration' (§2.15 black-box). The library's PRINCIPLES — the 14-type silence taxonomy across 2 stances (fillable / acknowledge; Decision 215) + the copyright fallback ladder (held / cited-not-held / rights-blocked; Decision 213) — render live on the principles page, the top-linked read-me.
stages.logic: IN: a clavis snapshot (external authority's enumeration) → BOX: set-difference vs corpus holdings, then LLM-adjudicate candidate matches (Haiku temp 0, every verdict logged) → OUT: recall % + a desiderata ticket per silence carrying its clavis_number → NEXT: GROW acquires the silence, the round-trip closes it.

status.coverage: 348 silences named · 322 carry a clavis URI
status.unit: one clavis entry with 0 corpus witnesses → one silence_finding ticket
status.limit: The CLAVIS has silences too: Syriaca.org does NOT enumerate gospel commentaries (0 works; even Ephrem's Diatessaron Commentary is absent). The choice of clavis determines which silences are visible — a validated audit is not one with no blind spots, but one whose blind spots are NAMED. Coverage so far: Syriac + Ethiopic authors + gospels-resurrection.

closure_modes.label: Closing a silence — two modes (S159, Decision 217)
closure_modes.recognition: The text is already held, even bundled inside an anthology/collection under a different title/authority. The held-check probes the actual passage TEXT (≥3 distinct co-occurring phrases via passages_fts), not just the name registry — so a work hiding inside a 3,500-passage anthology is found and LINKED (no fetch).
closure_modes.acquisition: Genuinely absent, or held only MEDIATED (quoted inside a secondary work). GROW fetches a public-domain primary, chunks it, and closes — upgrading mediated→clean-primary.
closure_modes.quality_axis: 'Held' is not binary: clean-PD (a PD edition/anthology) · mediated (quoted inside a secondary work — flagged, upgraded to a clean primary when load-bearing) · present-via-copyright (exists only through a copyright edition — cited, never a clean hold).
closure_modes.example: S159 gospels: the Gospel of the Egyptians + the Oxyrhynchus sayings of Thomas were already held inside a PD anthology (recognition); Papias — the earliest gospel-authorship witness — was held only inside an 1870s polemic, so a clean primary (Eusebius III.39) was acquired (acquisition).

fields.desc: what KIND of absence this is — and, via its STANCE, whether the acquisition engine TARGETS it (fillable) or the map only NAMES it honestly (acknowledge). stages.name: Give the instrument what we hold
stages.what: SERVE hands the instrument the held, chunked L4 passages it reads — the join between the library (stock) and the Grammar-of-Meaning engine (method).
stages.why: The instrument codes L4 anchors; SERVE is where a curated reading-set (a flower + its reception) is assembled from the corpus, not the whole 12.8M-passage store (code the CURATED set, not the corpus).
stages.logic: IN: a reading target (a seed + its reception) → BOX: select the held L4 passages for those sources → OUT: a passage-set the instrument codes → NEXT: the engine's SITUATE/ANALYZE stages.

status.output: a bounded L4 passage-set per reading
status.limit: SERVE is per-reading + manual today; there is no general 'serve any query' index yet — it is assembled per flower. Coding targets the curated set, never '% of corpus coded'.

stages.name: Close the silence, grow the stock
stages.what: GROW is the flywheel: a named silence becomes a desiderata ticket, ACQUIRE lands the source, and the round-trip closes the silence (status → held). The library grows toward its own audited gaps, not toward whatever was easiest to harvest.
stages.why: This is what makes the corpus self-correcting: it does not just hold, it grows along the vector its own LACUNA audit points at — the §2.8 bias-correction made operational.
stages.logic: IN: an open silence_finding (identified) → BOX: route its clavis_number/title through ACQUIRE's Parity fan → OUT: a landed source + the silence advanced to held → NEXT: recall re-measures, higher.

status.unit: one silence → one acquisition → one closed gap
status.limit: The round-trip is proven on small N; the filled_by_source_id FK gap (see LACUNA drawer) means the close is recorded on status but the source-link is not yet back-filled.

stages.name: Durably backed, dual-stored
stages.what: The corpus is dual-stored — authoritative Neon (Postgres) + a local SQLite mirror — and backed nightly to Backblaze B2. A migration lands in BOTH stores (Decision 144); a public 'held' count can't drift because it is guarded (Decision 182 / §2.13).
stages.why: A decade-scale corpus that lives on one consumer laptop is one disk failure from zero. Durability is a first-class library property, not an afterthought.
stages.logic: IN: any canonical write → BOX: apply_migration.py --neon-also (dual-store) + nightly B2 sync → OUT: authoritative Neon + SQLite safety-net + off-site B2 → NEXT: parity verified (Decision 147).

status.coverage: Neon authoritative + SQLite mirror + B2 nightly
status.output: a recoverable corpus (B2 hours-stale, local days-stale, Neon live)
status.unit: one canonical write → two stores + one off-site backup
status.limit: B2 is hours-stale (nightly); recovery-freshness must always check B2 before a local backup. Dual-store parity is verified periodically, not on every write.

example.label: SPEC — store-level (no single row)
example.tests: test_b2_backup_freshness spec (§13 Mechanism 8); apply_migration parity check (Decision 147).

fields.desc: durability is a store property, not a column.
fields.caveat: the honest limit is freshness (B2 nightly), not existence — check B2 before local recovery.
